version.changelog: Fix stale npm shared package dependency pins for baoyu-md and baoyu-chrome-cdp 0.1.1.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims, but it uses an authenticated browser, clipboard automation, process control, and an unpinned runtime download path that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Chrome CDP, persistent Chrome profile use, system clipboard writes, real paste keystrokes, file uploads, and local file reads are understandable for this workflow, but together they create a broad local and account-impacting execution surface.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no install script, but normal execution can fetch and run the mutable bun package through npx -y bun without a pinned version or integrity check. The included bun.lock pins script dependencies, not that runtime fallback.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions authorize automatic recovery by killing matching CDP Chrome processes without asking, and they direct agents to use npx -y bun when Bun is unavailable. Those actions are broader than simple content composition and are not tightly permissioned.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses that first-run login creates a persistent browser session, and it creates/reuses a Chrome profile for that purpose. I did not find backdoor-style persistence, though article HTML is written to a predictable temporary path and may remain after execution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently support composing Weibo regular posts and Markdown-based headline articles through Chrome CDP, with manual user review before final publishing. The capability is high impact because it operates inside an authenticated Weibo browser session and can upload user-selected media.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use a locally installed trusted Bun runtime instead of the npx fallback, run it with an isolated Chrome profile, and verify all content in the browser before publishing. Be cautious on shared machines because it uses the system clipboard, real paste keystrokes, authenticated Weibo session state, and a predictable temporary article file.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: helper scripts are utilities, and the broader artifact includes weibo-post, weibo-article, and md-to-html support matching the stated regular-post and article workflows.
[SDI-1] expected: Overridden: weibo-post.ts is only the regular-post path, while weibo-article.ts and md-to-html.ts implement the claimed headline article Markdown workflow.
[LP3] expected: Accepted as a scope concern: the documented workflow needs browser, filesystem, clipboard, and process execution, but the skill does not define narrow permission boundaries for those capabilities.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md and helper code allow npx -y bun, which can download and execute a mutable runtime package without a pinned version.
[EA2] expected: Accepted as limited but material: automatic termination is scoped to CDP Chrome instances using the baoyu profile, but it is still a host-side process action performed without confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in context: the process-kill pattern is narrower than killing all Chrome instances, but it remains disruptive if matching is wrong or unsaved browser state exists.
[T03] unexpected: Accepted: scripts/weibo-utils.ts runs npx -y bun for clipboard and paste helpers, creating a mutable remote-code execution path when Bun is not already installed.
[T09] unexpected: Partially accepted: paste-from-clipboard.ts exposes an unsanitized macOS --app argument in generated AppleScript, and weibo-article.ts uses a fixed shared temporary HTML file; both are implementation flaws rather than intended behavior.
